Hi Alex / Priya — happy to jump on a 30-min tech sync. Below are concise answers + example patterns we use; happy to expand in the call.

1) Ephemeral partner keys
- Pattern: Redwood issues a short-lived API token bound to a partner ID. Tokens are minted server-side and returned over TLS; the long-lived secret is stored only in the customer’s KMS or Redwood’s encrypted vault depending on the integration model.
- Recommended TTL: 1h–24h for partner-facing tokens, with refresh endpoints for long-lived sessions.

2) KMS/HSM integration
- We support: AWS KMS (Encrypt/Decrypt & Sign), GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and integration adapters for Vault HSM-backed storage.
- Options: 
  a) Customer-managed keys: Redwood calls customer KMS for signing (no plaintext key leaves KMS).
  b) Redwood-managed keys with CMK import: for customers who want Redwood to manage rotation but require importable CMKs.

3) Service-account JWT issuance (example)
- Typical flow: Customer service account credentials (stored in KMS/vault) are used to sign a JWT with claims {iss: "fintechco", sub: "service-account-123", aud: "redwood-inference", iat, exp}. Redwood validates aud/iss and issues a short-lived session token (opaque) for API calls.
- TTLs: session token 15m–1h; signed JWT lifetime can be short (5–30m) depending on use case.

4) Rotation + revocation
- Automated rotation: Redwood can perform rotation via scheduled jobs or on-demand via API.
- Revocation: we support immediate revocation and a configurable overlap window (default 5m) to replay in-flight requests. For higher-availability use cases, increase overlap to 1–2 minutes.

Migration checklist (high level):
- Inventory current keys -> export
- Classify keys by use-case (partner, batch, internal)
- Create scoped service accounts for batch jobs
- Implement short-lived tokens for partner SDKs and remove embedded long-lived keys
- Integrate with KMS for signing/storage; validate with test rotations
- Roll out revocation and monitoring + audit log verification

SDK snippets / links:
- Server (Node): mintToken example -> https://docs.redwood.ai/sdks/node#mint-token
- Rotation API: POST /v1/keys/rotate -> https://docs.redwood.ai/reference/keys#rotate

If helpful, I can draft a one-page security summary for your compliance team that explicitly maps to AWS KMS and Vault flows.
